$comment: Provider config — the single source of truth for the ADR-0009 vendor allowlist: endpoints, model ids, api-key env names, prices per MTok, and per-role fallback chains (ADR-0022). Vendor data lives ONLY here (and the model_configs DB mirror); no .ts file in the engine may name a vendor — the boundary gate enforces it by scanning .ts and not .json. Prices are micro-USD per MTok (1 USD = 1e6 micro-USD, so a $0.50/MTok input price is 500000), PR-reviewed like any model decision. Defaults from SPECS.md §3.4 (2026-08).

gemini-embedding-2.$comment: #9 benchmark challenger — explicitly cross-lingual (100+ languages); incompatible embedding space with embedding-001, so adopting it is a clean-slate re-embed, not an upgrade. Dimensions verified 1536 on the OpenAI-compat endpoint.

gemini-paid.$comment: The SAME Gemini API and the SAME model ids on PAID terms (standard tier, billing enabled, DPA-covered) — a separate vendor row because the register rule (ADR-0043 decision 3) keys on terms, not on the model: the free-tier row may never carry personal data, the paid row may. GEMINI_PAID_API_KEY is a distinct key on a billing-enabled Google project; an embedding served through this row uses the identical embedding space as the free-tier row, so the already-ingested corpus vectors (ADR-0036 gate winner) stay valid — no re-embed. Price: the currently published paid embedding input price for the Gemini embedding family ($0.20/MTok, ai.google.dev pricing, checked 2026-09-20); gemini-embedding-001's own paid price is no longer published separately.

typesafe.$comment: ADR-0042: TypeSafe AI 'System One' decision endpoint — typed structured questions (Choice/Score/Noul) over a state, priced on input tokens only (output free). Not a chat or embedding vendor: it backs the decision-bench role only until the multilingual gate is evaluated; serving adoption is a future ADR.

jev-1.13.0.$comment: Pinned version — 64k request / 32k state budget, 1,200 req/min. 42 micro-USD per input MTok (ADR-0042).

generator.$comment: Cost posture decided 2026-09-12 (ADR-0009 amendment): the answer generator runs on the cheap tier — DeepSeek V4-Flash at $0.14/$0.28 per MTok vs Qwen3.7-Max's $2.50/$7.50 — because the trust invariant is carried by the deterministic citation gate and the cross-vendor reviewer, not by generator price. The Qwen3.7-Max tail was REMOVED on 2026-09-12 (owner decision): DashScope is not provisioned and will not be, and resolveRole silently filters candidates whose apiKeyEnv is unset — so the chain advertised a failover that could never be wired. Single candidate, accepted single point of failure: a generator failure costs one <=$1 smoke re-run, not data. Re-adding a fallback means adding a candidate whose key is actually bound.

reviewer.$comment: Personal-data posture (ADR-0043 gap closure, #181; amended 2026-09-21 per owner): the serving reviewer's prompt embeds the user's question and the drafted answer, so with PromptSpec.personalData required on every serving call only a paid candidate may serve. The designed head was kimi:kimi-k2.6 (cross-vendor, ADR-0009/ADR-0015), but the owner holds no Moonshot key and elected (issue #181 thread) to remove Moonshot from the register and head the reviewer with the DeepSeek generator model instead. This accepts same-vendor review — the property ADR-0015 named 'anti-self-review' is relaxed for the current key set, recorded as a deliberate trade-off rather than drifted into. Revisit when a second paid vendor key (kimi, qwen) is provisioned.

reviewer-live.$comment: Same amendment as the reviewer chain: the live reviewer is DeepSeek until a second paid vendor key exists.

cheap.$comment: Router stages 1-3, tagging, cleaning. REORDERED for the personal-data posture (#181, ADR-0043 gap closure): the serving router prompt carries the user's question, so with PromptSpec.personalData required on serving calls the paid DeepSeek head answers them and the free-tier Gemini tail is skipped. Free tier remains available for non-personal calls (ingest summaries, tagging, cleaning — corpus text only). Cost: the router is 3 short calls per question, ~$0.001-0.005 per query at DeepSeek V4-Flash $0.14/$0.28 — the free-tier saving was never material.

embedder.$comment: Decided by the #9 embedding benchmark gate (ADR-0036): the chain holds the gate's winner only — never both models, they are embedding-space-incompatible. Moved to the PAID terms row (#181, ADR-0043 gap closure): the serving retriever embeds the user's sub-queries (personal data), so the free-tier row can no longer carry chat-path embeddings. gemini-paid:gemini-embedding-001 is the SAME model and embedding space on paid/DPA-covered terms — the corpus vectors stay valid, no re-embed. Corpus ingestion rides the same paid row (its texts are corpus content, not personal data, but one role keeps the config honest and removes the free-tier ~1,000 items/day wall ADR-0036 called 'infeasible' for full-corpus runs). Requires GEMINI_PAID_API_KEY to be bound (owner action, cited in #181's runbook).

embedder-candidates.$comment: #9 gate benchmark role: every candidate the benchmark compares, in one chain. Not for serving — the benchmark resolves each candidate directly from this chain (ADR-0022). Kept on the free-tier row: the benchmark embeds gate-fixture text, never personal data, and its per-candidate cost lines in the report were measured on those terms.

decision-candidates.$comment: ADR-0042 decision-bench role (mirrors embedder-candidates): every decision-model candidate the multilingual gate compares. Not for serving — the bench resolves each candidate directly. Absent key = the bench reports NOT RUN and exits 0 (CI has no JEV_API_KEY).
